title: Suspected stroke on the high street
setting: Friday night high street. Elderly person sitting on a bench, looking disoriented, slurring speech, face drooping, left arm weakness.
verdictExplanation: Positive FAST test (Face drooped, Arm weakness, Speech slurred). This is a suspected stroke, a time-critical neurological emergency. Sick: requires immediate 999 escalation.

history.history: Shopping in local high street, felt 'out of sorts' and sat down on bench 15 minutes ago
history.additional: Dribbling slightly, which he finds very embarrassing

followUp.question: Which of the following is the most critical piece of information to communicate to ambulance control for this patient?

options.text: The exact time the symptoms started, as this determines their eligibility for time-critical clot-busting treatments
The patient's blood pressure, as ambulance control will want you to administer their ramipril tablet
The fact that they are embarrassed by their drooling
Their blood glucose level, because a level of 7.9 mmol/L definitively confirms a stroke diagnosis

followUp.explanation: For a suspected stroke, noting and communicating the exact time of symptom onset is vital because thrombolysis (clot-busting medication) has a strict time window. Blood glucose should be checked to rule out a mimic (hypoglycaemia), but time of onset is the critical stroke-specific red flag to convey.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: FAST test positive. Call 999 immediately, keep calm, protect airway.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected acute stroke. Monitor airway. Check BGL to rule out hypoglycaemia. Administer oxygen if SpO₂ <94%. Prepare for rapid transport.
